'''Mario Hezonja''' (born 25 February 1995) is a Croatian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]] of the [[Liga ACB|ACB League]]. He also represents the [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national basketball team]] internationally. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=7+1/2}}, he primarily plays at the [[shooting guard]] position, but he can also play the [[small forward]] position. 

==Professional career==

===Early years===
Hezonja started playing basketball at the age of 13 in [[KK Dubrovnik|Dubrovnik]] where he stayed for two seasons. After finishing primary school, in 2010, Hezonja signed a contract with the Croatian club [[KK Zagreb|Zagreb]]. In 2011, he won the [[Nike International Junior Tournament]] with [[KK Zagreb|Zagreb]]. He was named into the All-Tournament team, alongside with then teammate [[Dario Šarić]]. He skipped the 2011–2012 season because of [[Infectious mononucleosis|mononucleosis]].

===Barcelona===
In July 2012, Hezonja signed a three-year contract with the Spanish club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Vera|first=Sergio|title=Hezonja, la gran perla que aterriza en Barcelona|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/acb/hezonja-gran-perla-que-aterriza-barcelona-2058742|language=Spanish|publisher=Sport.es|accessdate=11 July 2012}}</ref> He also has an option to extend for additional four years with the club. His former club Zagreb also got 150,000 [[euro]]s in the name of buyout, as he was still under contract. For the 2012–13 season, he was loaned to the [[reserve team]] of the club: [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet B|Barcelona B]] of the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|LEB Oro]], Spanish second division. In 2012, Hezonja was nominated for the [[FIBA Europe Young Men's Player of the Year Award|FIBA Europe Young Player of the Year Award]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/coid_MUMtgYLNGw6ts8a4RCdLp3.articleMode_on.html|title=Valanciunas Young Men’s POY 2012|publisher=FIBA Europe.com|date=6 February 2013|accessdate=20 February 2013}}</ref> but [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] eventually won the award.

Hezonja played in the [[2012–13 Euroleague|Euroleague]] for the first time in 2012–13 season. He appeared in only 2 games, averaging 2.5 points and 2 rebounds per game. In 2013, Hezonja was invited to be a part of the world team at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]], but couldn't attend because of injury. In 2013–14 season he became more constant part of the Barcelona's first team rotation, although playing very limited minutes.

Starting with the 2014–15 season, Hezonja's role in the team increased, from playing only in the [[garbage time]] in the previous season to around 15 minutes per game on constant basis.
On February 1, 2015, he hit 8 from 8 from the 3-point line in a 101–53 Barcelona's win against [[Bàsquet Manresa|La Bruixa d'Or Manresa]], becoming the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] MVP for the week 19.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=110483|title=Mario Hezonja, jugador de la jornada 19|language=Spanish|publisher=ACB.com|date=1 February 2015}}</ref> Barcelona finished the participation in the [[2014–15 Euroleague|Euroleague]] after quarterfinal series loss to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. Over 22 Euroleague games played, Hezonja averaged 7.7 points, 2 rebounds and 1 assist per game.

On April 23, 2015, he declared himself eligible for the [[2015 NBA Draft]] as an international "early-entrant", only day after the Barcelona's elimination in the Euroleague.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vecenie|first1=Sam|title=Croatian wing Mario Hezonja to declare for 2015 NBA Draft|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/25161381/croatian-wing-mario-hezonja-to-declare-for-2015-nba-draft|accessdate=24 April 2015|work=cbssports.com}}</ref> Some Spanish and 2015|language=Spanish}}</ref>

==Croatian national team==
Hezonja was named Most Valuable Player of the [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], after leading his team with a double-double in the final, 21 points, 10 rebounds and 3 steals.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.coid_FxtbjQqyId2WVafytY6os2.articleMode_on.html |title=Super Mario Leads Croatia to Gold|first=Dan|last=Casey|publisher=FIBA Europe.com |date=7 August 2011 }}</ref> Over the tournament, he averaged 20 points, 8.2 rebounds and 2.7 assists.

He was part of the senior [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national basketball team]] at the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]].
